inventory.note: What the town ALREADY CONTAINS, in the words a brief would use. Read by every worker before it builds. This list is the direct antidote to the previous loop's terminal failure mode: nine consecutive iterations that each surveyed the world, found everything already existed, and exited.
courtyard: walled garden with an organic bed ring
four arch entrances (two TUNNEL, two SLOT)
planting CA with 11 species and bloom stages
seeds that spread from mature neighbours, and beds that crowd out and die back with age
rain that accelerates every growth term

the planting CA reads the YEAR — growF() 0.30..1.70, dieF() 1.80..0.20 and bloomCap() 3/2/1 (thresholds warmth 0.42/0.20), all off b11's warmth and each equal to the constant it replaced at warmth 0.5; they scale both seed rolls, the stage advance, wear recovery, the daisy terms and the dieback probability. bloomCap is a CEILING not a kill term — caTick already ages whatever sits at its ceiling, so lowering it empties the beds by itself. Per-cell hardiness hash(x,y+41)>0.86 keeps ~1/7 of cells at the full ceiling so deep winter is a scatter of blooms (17-35) in turned earth, never zero. blooming traces 17..698 over the 26-day year; the species mix holds at Shannon evenness ~0.998 across three years because winter forces fresh draws (neighborsMature finds nothing to inherit). Lawn health in groundCol and the gatehouse ivy reach+colour read the same warmth instead of deriving from richness(); ivy clamped to 5.2 against a measured 5.6 eave. probes/beds-year.mjs
lane: washing lines strung over the lane
market day every 4th day with three stalls
washing that comes in before the rain — per-garment thresholds and ~1.6s fades on weatherComing() plus a dusk ramp, never all in one frame

market stalls put up and packed away — marketRaise(i), a per-stall staggered 0..1 progress (6.90-8.00 up, 17.00-18.10 down) staging trader/trestle/frame/canvas/goods as clamps on it; marketActive() still owns the open hours; the ticker brackets the day
street: cross street with two footways, roadway, curbs
allotment block of 17 plots (buildGrid excludes the pond corner), timber fence, gates, shed
an alley cut through the block
allotment harvest cycle — harvestPlot() lifts a mature 3x2 bed whole, bAge doubles as a 12-20s fallow clock, then it is re-sown as a row under plotCrop()
spawnAllotAgent() — the allotments own arrival source, rate scaling on ripePlots(); ~1.1 gardeners/day, ~1 plot cleared/day
gardeners work 1-3 rows a visit and walk out carrying a basket of the crop (a.crop)
plaza: quay along the river with benches

spawnEastAgent() — the east quarter own arrival source (eastCap/eastRate, a.east, excluded from laneCount); enters by the alley, the quay head or the park gate, visits one stop, leaves the way it came; eastOpen() on daylight>0.16
river: pigeons that flush off the belfry when the bell rings, from a finite roost that refills

the boat is watched — boatWatch() gives anyone byTheWater() (quay and rail, bridge deck, towpath) one glance per boat (a.watch, ~1.4s, ticked at the top of stepAgent so it never holds anybody); drawPerson tracks the live boat and standers turn. ~2.1 glances per boat
a parapet stop mid-span (PARAPET_Y, PARAPET_Z 1.0), served mainly from spawnEastAgent; somebody is on the bridge ~12% of daylight
sky: cloudCover() — one slow rate-capped scalar; fronts build over ~half a day and break after rain, rain is gated on it so it never rains from a clear sky, sun and moon veiled, stars put out, drifting cloud banks
weatherComing() — one ramped rain-is-coming predicate off cloudCover(), damped by daylight so overcast nights read 0; three readers at their own trigger points

season() — the town's YEAR: one slow CYCLIC scalar over SEASON_LEN 26 days (~24 real min), phase 0 = midwinter, clock starts at 0.25 where warmth = 0.5 and every seasoned term equals the constant it replaced. Rate-capped by construction (7.0e-4/s), continuous through the wrap. Two sky readers — day length (dayHours 11.5..17.5 about SOLAR_NOON 12.75; sunUp/sunDown/sunArc/timeLabel) and light (sunVec elevation + azimuth, the drawn disc's arc height and colour, skyCols day/night/dusk palettes with both dusk windows hung off sunset/sunrise, the roof key term 0.84..1.16). Population breathes ~15% trough-to-peak, absolute floor 7 people. census clock.season

rainFall — a 0..1 shower intensity beside the raining boolean; drops, the overcast tint, pond rings, water sparkle and chimney smoke all read it, so a shower thins out over RAIN_TAIL=2.2s instead of cutting
life: walkers with itineraries, courtyard and street
eastern itineraries: plaza bench, fountain gaze, quay rail, quay bench, towpath, church green, allotment plot, bridge parapet
cafe sitters who claim and release a table
market and kiosk browsers
ducks
swans
butterflies (capped drift, 3 cells/s)
fireflies
birds
one night cat
falling leaves
a clock that strikes and a church bell that answers it at nine and eighteen from day 2
an ambient ticker
walkers who break stride and look up while the bell rings (a.listen)
agents that notice each other — two passing within 0.9-1.6 cells may stop, turn and talk (greetPass, a.greet, chatCool); ~2 conversations a minute
street sitters who read the sky (refuse above weatherComing() 0.42, released over 0.55..0.88 off a per-agent a.wary); courtyard sitters excluded
umbrellas up over weatherComing() 0.62..1.17, so ~30% get caught out

THE DIORAMA IS ALREADY CLICKABLE and nothing on screen says so — cv click + unproject(): a bed takes a handful of a real species, the lawn takes a daisy, the pond takes crumbs and the ducks converge like a small navy, the fountain takes a coin, the river takes a pebble, the lane takes crumbs and birds land. Built pre-loop, never advertised, and the coverage grid reads interaction=0 which is about the LOOP, not the town
__entities() carries role, act and watch per person — the seam a behaviour probe reads instead of a bespoke hook
the ticker is an ordered queue, not an overwrite — TICK_DWELL 2.5 real seconds per line, cap 2, 6 s staleness cut, and a follow-on line is enqueued only when its antecedent is DISPLAYED

the click is now ADVERTISED — answersTouch(x,y) is the ONE predicate for 'this cell answers' (BED/CBED/GRASS/WATER/SIDE/ROAD): the cursor swaps to pointer on it (46% of the frame) and the click handler guards on it; plus ONE ticker invitation, once ever, offered at 8 REAL seconds when tickerFree(), cancelled if the viewer clicks first (touched) and stood down on a ?pause page (DRIVEN). A narrow sill lends it the plate's and clock's place for 7 s (#sill.inviting) with a shorter line. probes/touch-hint.mjs
a ticker line may buy its own dwell — lineDwell + tickerFree(); the invitation takes 5.5 s where a remark gets TICK_DWELL 2.5 s

openCues.note: The town still casts hard sun shadows under full overcast — drawSunMoon veils the disc, but the ~6 SUN[0]/SUN[2] shadow call sites use fixed alphas.
Rain requires daylight>0.15, so a heavy front peaking overnight builds full cover, never rains, and breaks by morning — overcast nights are commoner than rain.
chatCool is decremented only inside greetPass(); an early-out there would freeze the cooldown
East agents retrace their inbound route exactly, so arrivals sharing a gate walk single-file; would queue if eastCap rose much above 7

Courtyard sitters (picnic, sitter kinds) do not read the sky — only a.street agents do. Their sit is assigned at a waypoint with no route left, so refusing it would despawn them mid-lawn; extending the effect inland needs routeToExit() on refusal.
ripePlots() rescans 102 cells every spawn tick (1/s) to set an arrival rate — the first place a spawn rate reads the CA. Free at this size; cache it on the CA tick if anything else wants the pattern.
marketRaise is the third hand-rolled staged-appearance clamp chain (washing, umbrellas, stalls); a fourth would justify a shared helper

byTheWater() names the three places a person can see the river. Only boatWatch reads it; any future river event (a swan taking off, ice, a barge) should read the same predicate rather than re-deriving it.

stall.mjs:110 and build-stats.mjs average secs/costUsd across all rows including the nine zero-metric ones, so the per-iteration means read low until rows with secs===0 are excluded from the aggregates

LAWS.md's probe law blames an unanchored .gitignore line that has never existed; the real #9 fault was a second probes/ directory at the repo root. Advice right, stated cause wrong — reword before it is re-derived.

stall.mjs's streak() runs over ALL rows, so manager passes (always verdict=no-ship, always srcChanged=false) count toward noShipStreak and srcFlat. With MANAGER_GAP=2 a manager row sits next to worker rows regularly, so ONE no-ship worker iteration is enough to fire both signals and summon a manager. Fired exactly that way at #11. Fix is to streak over kind==='worker' rows only — but it changes when the manager is summoned, so it is the manager's call.

capacity/laneCap/eastCap compress daylight hard (0.25+0.75*d), so a 52% swing in mean daylight moves capacity only 8->9 — that compression, not the season, caps the population breathing at ~15%. Widening it risks the winter floor; People & animals vector, manager's call.
stepClouds' heavy-front probability reads richness(), which pins at day 16 — weather is now the last slow system still on a one-way ramp. season() is available to it.

shoot.mjs runs ?fast with a fixed 2600ms wall wait, so its sim instant jitters ~15s and its --t comment is wrong; it shot 'Day 4 Night' twice while aiming at day-3 mid-morning. Fine as a smoke test, cannot compare two builds. probes/year-shots.mjs pins with ?pause+__warp.

A SIDE/ROAD click ANYWHERE in town announces the LANE crumb line and clamps the birds it spawns into the lane rows, so a cross-street or east-quarter click keeps its promise in the wrong place. Pre-existing, but the new pointer cursor is what makes it visible.
context-budget.mjs read OVER at 51.5 KB against the 46 KB cap when iteration 13 started; LEDGER.md at 18.6 KB is the bulk, laws 28/60.

The census age ladder conflates growth with season: its warp-900 'fully grown' cell lands at season 0.879 / warmth 0.14, i.e. midwinter. Iteration 14's whole -16.3% planted collapse is that one cell (the warp-90 and warp-330 cells were bit-unchanged), and a real winter planting regression is now invisible behind it. Pick ages at comparable warmth, or hold season fixed across the age axis.

The allotments now inherit bloomCap too (one shared caTick path, no special case), so crops do not ripen in deep winter, harvestPlot stops firing and ripePlots()->0 damps the allotment arrival source for ~a fifth of the year. Intended and seasonally true, but unmeasured over a full year — nobody has checked whether the gardeners come back at the right rate in spring.

shoot.mjs --tag is a no-op: it forwards --prefix to a screenshot-verify that ignores it, so two tagged runs silently overwrite each other's courtyard.png. Iteration 14 lost a summer shot to a winter one this way before noticing. Either implement the prefix or drop the flag.
motion.mjs tracks no raindrop kind, so the continuity gate cannot see the town's largest spawn/despawn population at all

The rain tail runs ~3s not RAIN_TAIL=2.2s: want falls to zero on a ramp but a drop only leaves when it reaches the bottom, so the count lags by one fall time (~1.4s). Tune the constant knowing it is not the duration.

watch.note: The whole east half is fed by a single spawnLaneAgent roll under one laneCap. Anything you add out there competes for that one budget — check whether your feature needs its own before you conclude nobody uses it. The bands, measured: cross-street diversion 0.30 of all spawns, then market 0.24, kiosk 0.18, café 0.26, allotment to 0.48, plaza to 0.48, quay 0.48-0.53, green 0.53-0.58. laneCap peaks at 9 in full daylight.

An empty-looking place is a budget question before it is a content question. Twice at pass #0 a plausible 'the town lacks X' turned out to be 'the town has X and you rarely see it' — the allotment gardeners and every eastern destination both exist. Grep for the feature before briefing it, and if it exists, ask how often it fires.

cloudCover() (added #3) is a slow world scalar with exactly ONE reader — the rain roll. It hands the town ~27 s of warning that rain is coming and nothing else in the file reads it. Any future weather work should ask whether it can read cover instead of reading `raining`, which is a boolean that flips in a single frame.
